questions.question: What is the chemical name of plaster of paris?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Plaster of Paris**/**Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate (CaSO₄·1/2H₂O):**

__
 
• It is a **white powdery substance** that is commonly **used **in the **medical field for casting broken bones.**
 
• It is **created by heating gypsum**, **a mineral found in sedimentary rocks.**
 
• When m**ixed with water, it forms a paste that hardens quickly** and is used in construction for creating molds and sculptures.
 
• It is a**lso used in the food industry as a coagulant** for tofu and as a calcium supplement in certain types of bread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calcium hypochlorite (Ca(ClO)₂):**

 
 
• It is a white solid, although commercial samples appear yellow.
 
• It is commonly **used to sanitize public swimming pools **and **disinfect drinking water.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃):**
 
 
• Similar to the minerals calcite and aragonite, it is a common component** found in rocks**, particularly in **chalk **and limestone, **eggshells**, gastropod shells, **shellfish skeletons**, and **pearls**.
 
• It is the **primary component of agricultural lime** and is created when carbonate ions and calcium ions in hard water combine to form limescale.
 
• It has **medical use** as a **calcium supplemen**t or as an antacid.
 
 
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• It is commonly known as **quicklime or burnt lime.**
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid at room temperature.
 
• It is used in the **production of cement, paper, and steel.**

questions.question: The time period of ______ year(s) is taken into account in calculating national income.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__one.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National income** of a country means the **sum total of incomes earned by the citizens of that country** during a given **period, over a year.**
 
• The** time period taken into account in calculating national income is usually one year or a fiscal year,** which is the period for which a company or government prepares its financial statements.
 
 
• However, in some cases, a longer period of two years is taken into account to account for fluctuations in economic activity due to seasonal factors, natural disasters, or other exceptional events.
 
• This longer period helps to smooth out the impact of short-term fluctuations and provides a more accurate picture of the overall economic performance of the country.
 
 
 
• **National income **is an important **indicator of a country's economic performance** and is used by policymakers, investors, and analysts to make decisions about economic policies and investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income is calculated using various methods**, such as the output method, income method, and expenditure method.

 
 
• **The output method** measures national income by** adding up the value of all goods and services produced** in the country, while the income method measures it by adding up all the income earned by individuals and businesses in the country.
 
• **The expenditure method** measures national income by **adding up all the spending on goods and services** by households, businesses, and the government.
 
• The** income method** measures all the** income earned by all the factors of production** in an economy.

• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP):**

• The **Bharatiya Jana Sangh**, founded in **1951 **by **Syama Prasad Mookerjee**, is where the BJP got its start.
 
• The Jana Sangh combined with a number of other parties to establish the Janata Party following the declaration of a state of emergency in 1977.

• **Since 2014**, it has been the** ruling political party in India** under the incumbent Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
 
 
• **The Indian National Congress (INC):**
 
 
• Retired British Indian Civil Service (ICS) officer Allan Octavian Hume founded the Indian National Congress to form a platform for civil and political dialogue among educated Indians.
 
• It was established on December 28th, 1885, with the presence of 72 delegates at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Mumbai, then known as Bombay.
 
• Prominent delegates included Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, W. C. Bonnerjee, S. Ramaswami Mudaliar, S. Subramania Iyer, and Romesh Chunder Dutt.
 
• Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee became its first president.
 
 
 
• **Communist Party of India (CPI):**
 
 
• It is a **left-wing political party **in India, founded in **1920 **in **Tashkent **(now the capital of **Uzbekistan**).
 
• **M.N. Roy** was the first elected Commintern leader.
 
• The CPI was **formally founded in 1925** at the Indian Communist Conference in **Kanpur.**
 
• It declared that revolution would be used to build socialism in India.
 
• Ideological differences led to the **split in the party in 1964** when two different party conferences were held, one of CPI and one of the **Communist Party of India (Marxist).**
 
 
 
• **Nationalist Congress Party (NCP):**
 
 
• It was **formed on 10 June 1999**, by **Sharad Pawar**,** P. A. Sangma**, and **Tariq Anwar **after they were expelled **from the Indian National Congress (INC).**
 
• In general, the party is in favor of **Gandhian secularism** and **Indian nationalism.**
 
• It is the **main political party** in **Kerala**, **Maharashtra**, and **Nagaland**, as well as **one of the state parties in India**.

questions.question: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Amendment) Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**February 4, 2021.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Amendment) Bill, 2021** was **introduced **in the** Rajya Sabha on February 4, 2021.**
 
• The bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2021, and by the Lok Sabha on February 13, 2021, and received the President's assent on March 28, 2021.
 
• The bill **seeks to amend the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019.**
 
 
• The amendments **proposed **in the bill include **changes to the composition of the Legislative Council of Jammu and Kashmir**, which was abolished in 2019, and the **reservation of seats in the Legislative Assembly for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019:**

 
• **On August 5, 2019**, the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation ACT, 2019 was **approved**, **dividing **the** region into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir **and **Ladakh.**
 
• The Act also **repealed Article 370**, which had granted **Jammu and Kashmir special status.**
 
• **On October 31, 2019**, the day of Sardar **Vallabhbhai Patel's birth**, which is observed as **National Unity Day**, **it came into force.**
 
• **Five Lok Sabha seats in Jammu and Kashmir** were retained by the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, while **one was transferred to the Union Territory of Ladakh.**

questions.question: Ashoka mentions in his inscription that he conquered Kalinga _________ after becoming the king.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eight years.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Mauryan Empire**:

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya **was the **founder **of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He is referred to in Greek sources as **Sandrokottos.**
 
• In 321 BC, he **defeated Dhana Nanda **and took the throne with the aid of a politically astute and clever Brahmin named **Kautilya**.
 
• **Megasthenes **served as the Greek representative in the court of Chandragupta.
 
• He led an expansionist policy that subjugated nearly all of modern-day India, **except **a few isolated areas in the far south and **Kalinga.**
 
• **Bindusara **is the second Mauryan Empire ruler.
 
• 297–273 BC was his rule period.
 
• He was also called **Amitraghata** (Slayer of foes).
 
• **Ashoka mentions in his inscription **that he **conquered Kalinga after becoming the king for eight years.**
 
• **Kalinga **was a region located in **present-day Odisha **and parts of **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• Ashoka established **Ujjain and Takshashila **(later Taxila) as the **regional capitals **of his kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Ashoka Maurya:**

 
• He was one of the **most powerful emperors of the Maurya dynasty **in ancient India, **ruling from 268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• The **conquest of Kalinga **was a major event in Ashoka's reign as it **resulted in the loss of over 100,000 lives **and left many more injured and displaced.
 
• He became deeply remorseful and **turned to Buddhism a****fter the war**, adopting a policy of non-violence and compassion towards all living beings.
 
• His **rock edicts and inscriptions**, which were written in various languages including Prakrit and Greek, **provide valuable insights into his life and teachings.******
 
• He designated representatives, referred to as the **dhamma mahamatta**, to spread the word and instruct people in dhamma.
 
• He also sent his children to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism.

questions.question: ______ is a crop that is used as both food and fodder. It is a Kharif crop which requires a temperature between 21°C to 27°C and grows well in old alluvial soils.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**corn.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Corn:**

__
 
• It is a crop that is **used as both food and fodder.**
 
• It is a **Kharif crop which requires a temperature of 21°C to 27°C.**
 
• It **grows well in old alluvial soils**, which are formed by the deposition of sediment by rivers.
 
• It is also **used for making ethanol, starch**, and other industrial products.
 
• It requires annual rainfall of 50 cm to 100 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Rice:**

 
• **It is a Kharif crop **that requires a temperature between 20°C to 37°C. 
 
• It grows well in **clayey loam soil**.​
 
• It is submerged under 5 to 10 cm of water.
 
• It contains riboflavin, iron, calcium, thiamine, and niacin.
 
• **India **is the world's **second-largest producer **of rice.

**Jute:**

 
• It is a **Kharif crop **that is grown in the rainy season and requires a temperature of **24°C to 35°C.**
 
• It grows well in **fertile, well-drained, and sandy loam soils**.
 
• It is an important natural fibre crop in India.
 
• It is a component of textiles used to package a variety of industrial and agricultural goods.
 
• It needs an **average monthly rainfall **of at least 7.5 to 10 cm.

**Wheat:**

 
• It is a **Rabi crop **that requires a temperature between **10°C to 15°C.**
 
• It grows well in **loamy soils**.
 
• It needs areas that receive between 30 and 90 cm of rainfall annually.
 
• It is used in industry for producing gluten, starch, malt, and alcohol.
 
• **India **is the world's **second-largest producer** of wheat.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an environmental factor that determines the rate of release of nutrients from the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**population.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Effects of Population on Environment:**

__
 
• An increase in **population puts an increasing amount of strain on the environment**, resulting in biodiversity loss, water scarcity, air pollution, and global warming.
 
• It **does not determine the rate of release of nutrients **from the atmosphere directly.
 
• It causes the **depletion of resources **in the areas of land use, water use, energy consumption, demand for food, and agricultural techniques.
 
• It also puts **strain on non-renewable resources **and extraction of minerals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Environmental factors that determine the rate of release of nutrients from the atmosphere are:**

**Heat:**

 
• **High temperatures** can **increase the rate of nutrient release **because it speeds up the decomposition of organic matter.
 
• Low temperatures can slow it down.
 
• **Extremely high temperatures **can also lead to the **loss of nutrients **through volatilization.

**Humidity:**

 
• **High humidity **can **increase the rate of nutrient release** because it creates a favorable environment for microbial activity.
 
• Low humidity can slow it down.
 
• **Excessive moisture** can also **lead to leaching of nutrients.**

**Precipitation:**

 
• The amount and frequency of Precipitation can affect the rate of nutrient release.
 
• **Heavy Precipitation**** **can **lead to leaching of nutrients.**
 
• Low Precipitation can result in nutrient deficiency.

**Soil:**

 
• **Soil** particles have the ability to **adsorb and desorb nutrients.**
 
• Nutrients like **ammonium (NH₄⁺)**,** nitrate (NO₃⁻), and phosphate (PO₄³⁻) **can be adsorbed onto soil particles and later released back into the soil solution.
 
• This process **affects** the availability of **nutrients **in the soil and their **potential release into the atmosphere**.
 
• **Soil pH **can impact nutrient availability.
 
• For example, sandy soil tends to release nutrients more quickly than clay soil.

questions.question: ____, keep stock in the warehouse for the retailers so that the goods can be made available to the retailers whenever they need them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wholesaler.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Wholesalers:**

__
 
• They are** intermediaries** who buy goods in bulk from manufacturers and sell them to retailers or other businesses.
 
• They act as a **link between the manufacturer and the retailer **and help in distributing the goods to the end customers.
 
• They usually **keep a large inventory **of goods in their warehouse **so that they can fulfill the orders of retailers quickly.**
 
• They often provide other services like **transportation, packaging, and labeling of goods.**
 
• They **also help in marketing **the products and provide valuable **feedback to the manufacturers **regarding the demand and supply of goods in the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Buyers:**

 
• They** **are individuals or businesses that **purchase goods for their personal or business use.**
 
• They do not usually keep a large inventory of goods in their warehouse and **buy goods in small quantities **as per their requirements.

**Customers:**

 
• They** **are **end-users **who purchase goods for their personal use.
 
• They do not usually buy goods in large quantities and **depend on the retailers to provide them with the desired products.**

**Sellers:**

 
• They** **are **individuals **or businesses who offer goods for sale.
 
• They may or may not keep stock in their warehouse and **often rely on intermediaries like wholesalers, retailers, or online marketplaces to sell their products**.

questions.question: Which of the following folk dance styles is not related to the state of Haryana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rauf.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rauf **is a traditional folk dance form that **hails from the region of Jammu and Kashmir** in northern India.
 
• It originated within the **Muslim community** and was **performed by women.**
 
• This dance is **performed **to commemorate the **arrival of spring **and to emulate the joy that pervades other **Muslim holidays, such as Eid-ul-Fitr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Fag**:

 
• The dance is **performed** by the people **in Haryana**.
 
• It is **performed in the lunar month of Phalgun**.
 
• It is performed in the **Dhamal style **of Haryana.
 
• It is performed by both **men and women.**

**Gugga:**

 
• This dance is also a folk **dance from Haryana.**
 
• It was **named **by the devotees of **Saint Dugga.**
 
• Performers are carrying a long, sturdy** bamboo staff that is adorned with fans, garlands, and colorful cloth**.

**Khoriya:**

 
• In **Haryana's central region**, this dance is popular.
 
• It is **linked **to both people's **everyday activities **and the most significant occasions, such as **harvests and agricultural labor, etc.**
 
• Performers wear finely embroidered golden-thread skirts, vibrantly colored dupattas that resemble veil-like garments, and substantial rustic jewelry.
